proposal.for: the primary/supervisor - needs arrival-list admission before any lane or worker may land it
proposal.file: src/repository_presenter/core/llm/jobs.py::_parse (line ~368, the `if not errors and checks is not None:` guard)
proposal.root_cause: Domain checks (plan_checks, unit_checks, and any other job's `checks` callable) only ever run when core/llm/binding.py::binding_errors already found nothing wrong with that attempt's citations. An attempt that has both kinds of defect at once reports only the binding one; the domain defect stays invisible until a later attempt happens to clear the binding defect - by which point core/llm/jobs.py's universal one-re-ask budget (unchanged by PGPY-01/item 95, and not proposed for change here either) is already spent, so a defect the improved message (item 95) could have let the model fix in one shot is never shown to it in time.
proposal.proposed_shape: Run `checks(output)` unconditionally whenever `checks is not None` (in addition to, not instead of, `binding_errors`), and merge both lists into one rejection, so a single re-ask attempt can see and address every defect the attempt actually has, not just whichever check family happened to be evaluated. planning.py's plan_checks is already safe to call on a payload with an unresolvable fact_id (its citation lookups default silently via `.get(i, "")`, verified by reading lines 664-668 this session); authoring.py's unit_checks was not read line-by-line this session and should be confirmed equally defensive before landing this - flagged for whoever lands it, not assumed. No new blocking check (rule 14) and no relaxation of any existing one - the change only affects which attempt's rejection text a defect's message appears in, never whether the defect is eventually enforced.
proposal.explicitly_not_proposed: NO increase to the one-re-ask budget in core/llm/jobs.py (PGPY-01's own scoping reasoning applies unchanged: a materially bigger, costlier, more universal lever, not measured necessary here - a well-informed single re-ask may already be enough once it can see the whole picture). NO change to binding_errors' own rules or to what plan_checks/unit_checks consider a title-terms violation - only to the order in which the two check families run relative to each other.
